newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods weak late in day, NYMEX paces losses.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods weak late in day, NYMEX paces losses.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products ended lower Wednesday, paced by the sharp decline in NYMEX futures prices.

Traders pointed to the large builds in refined products in the American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration inventory reports as bearish factors, as well as the return of Iraqi oil to the world market and the modest heating oil demand in the Northeast, the key usage area.
Differentials ended the day mixed, with U.S. Gulf (USG) No. 2 heating oil and gasoline easing versus the screen while New York Harbor conventional gasoline firmed.
USG heating oil differentials weakened slightly, with traders quoting offers for nearby barrels at 5.00 cents under the screen, down about 0.5 cent from Tuesday.
Low sulphur diesel also dipped, with nearby material talked between 4.75 and 5.00 cents under the NYMEX.
Back 35th cycle M4 conventional unleaded gasoline on the Colonial Pipeline traded earlier at 5.50 cents under the print and was now bid at about 5.75 cents under, down about 0.25 cent on the day.
But premium 93-octane gasoline for back 35th cycle on the Colonial was done at 3.00 cents above conventional barrels.
